exDef.label: Recipient not available
exDef.desc: Nobody available to accept or sign.

items.label: Calmed an upset customer
items.feedback: Acknowledge first, then offer something real. Most anger is about not being heard.

items.label: Moved a heavy package on the hand truck
items.lesson: Anything 50 lb or more goes on the hand truck (or gets a second person). Don't carry what you can wheel.

items.label: Climbed down from the cab with three points of contact
items.lesson: Use three points of contact getting in and out of the truck. Jumping down is one of the most common ways couriers get hurt.

items.label: Climbed back into the cab safely
items.lesson: Grab handle, one step at a time, and never jump up while carrying anything.

items.label: Delivered the correct package
Scanned the package before leaving the truck
items.lesson: Scan before you step out. It confirms the stop and shows signature needs before you walk to the door.

items.label: Scanned every package delivered
Chose the right way to deliver
items.lesson: Acknowledge the problem, apologize for the experience, offer the next step. Then the signature.

items.label: Recorded the signer's real printed name
items.lesson: Record the printed name of whoever actually signed, even if that isn't the addressee.

items.label: Finished the stop in good time (34s, par 150s)
items.lesson: Plan the stop before you step out: package pulled, scanned and ready. It saves walks back to the truck.

items.label: Pulled only the right package from the shelves

items.feedback: The label, pointing and the screen do the talking. A couple of words of the customer's language are a kindness, not a requirement.

Kept a signature package from someone who isn't the customer
items.feedback: Polite and firm. The rule protects Priya, and a friendly stranger is exactly who it protects her from.

items.label: Climbed down from the cab with three points of contact
items.lesson: Use three points of contact getting in and out of the truck. Jumping down is one of the most common ways couriers get hurt.

items.label: Climbed back into the cab safely
items.lesson: Grab handle, one step at a time, and never jump up while carrying anything.

items.label: Scanned the package before leaving the truck
items.lesson: Scan before you step out. It confirms the stop and shows signature needs before you walk to the door.

items.label: Recorded the right exception (NA)
items.lesson: Nobody home + signature required = exception, a door tag, and the package stays with you. Whoever offers to take it.

items.label: Left a door tag for the customer
items.lesson: When a delivery attempt fails, leave a door tag so the customer knows what happened and what to do next.

items.label: Kept the package secure on the truck
items.lesson: After an exception the package goes back on the truck. Never leave it behind.

items.label: Made a real attempt before the exception
items.lesson: Knock or ring and wait a moment before recording that nobody was available.

items.label: Finished the stop in good time (37s, par 150s)
items.lesson: Plan the stop before you step out: package pulled, scanned and ready. It saves walks back to the truck.

items.label: Pulled only the right package from the shelves

lessons: An upset customer calms down faster when you acknowledge the problem first and then say what you can do.
A language barrier is solved with the label, pointing and the handheld's screen, not by talking louder.
A signature-required package goes only to the person who can sign for it. A helpful neighbor is still not the customer.
Heavy packages go on the hand truck (or get a second person): don't carry what you can wheel.

scope: Only existing-id registration and a real suspended workday are fixtures. All movement, aiming, parcels, replies, signatures and tag attachment use real keys. No position, node, timer, signature completion, score or verdict fixtures. Larger Tamil assessments choose the authored neighbor critical.
